spans.text: ## Request

Compare the actual prior and current TDG publication bundles for CP-8 run `sol-tdg-cp8-delivery-comparison-20261105`, method `deploy-v-r14`, executed **November 5, 2026**. Prior publication run: `cpos-sol-medium-20261105-pathway`; current publication run: `sol-fresh-tdg-complete-20261105` (each `view.json`, chunk 1, `run.run_id`; corroborated by the original CP-1/CP-2 Requests).

**Bottom line:** the current deliverable expands a five-panel historical report into a twelve-panel publication, corrects source interpretation and adds instrument-specific legal, conditional security-comparison, evidence-QA and committee work. The sampled core annual financial quantities and calculation definitions are unchanged. This is the **same September 30, 2024 accounting base**, not a new financial period or evidence of deterioration between publication runs. The current committee's “Requires More Work” is an added historical analytical conclusion, not a downgrade from an available prior investment decision.
## Sources
### Coverage and assurance boundary

The pinned inventory contains complete bundles. My review used two batched evidence turns: both delivery receipts in full; both `report-view.json` and `model-report-view.json` chunk 1; both `calculation.json` chunks 3–5; original CP-1 and CP-2 chunk 1 on both sides; current CP-5 chunk 1 and CP-6 chunk 4; targeted searches in original CP-1A, current CP-0/CP-3/CP-4/CP-6, both view records and Model records; and chunk 27 of all four report/Model HTML files. Here **chunk** means a 12,000-character tool page, not a physical document page. Original handoff citations to S1 PDF pages are inherited source lineage, not a claim that CP-8 reopened the PDF.

The supplied host validation checked **both complete bundles and their HTML/view bindings**. That is broader than my sampled reads. My HTML sample establishes the report-destination shell (`nav#rail`, `#rail-dests`, `#rail-foot`), Model/report shell consistency and chart/inspector implementation text; the link searches returned the `#workbench` skip link, not a full independent destination audit. Actual publication destinations/bindings therefore rely on the supplied host validation together with receipt/view evidence, not a claimed exhaustive CP-8 HTML audit. Extracted JSON/HTML is **not independent visual browser assurance**. I did not compare every record, render the pages, test interactions or independently rehash files.
### Immutable publication anchors
Exact pinned SHA-256 identities (prior → current):
- **Delivery receipts**, `delivery.json`, chunk 1: `4ef9641a0cd8d5b4de2930c027badc2a4b1e5bf3ba9dba8e6ec015543b40f1f2` → `08235108827b82ccdf103acfe74ccae5144ec38873bf9a6b916f9597b481f285`.

- **Calculation JSON**, `calculation.json`: `1fcbe7788cef0cf523ab3a1dc4dbd506951d5bca8c7a82f92b9458e4fea12797` → `437004d244f2d3a351620498a1a7d8b60901ea72dbbca9d13c09de3d0eda5ab1`.
- **Published Models**, `model.html`: `c35a5a7ff94d55ee06fed28733c30201c74df59f760d97cafcabf912dd888a53` → `b7148844ffb307675ce58e0da088c2ff2fb04c9ebd460301e8f21c94e835642e`.
